is_anopheles.evidence: We investigated pyrethroid resistance in four populations of An. arabiensis from south-western Ethiopia (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper refers to kdr-L1014F and ace-1R as previously identified mutations from prior published studies (references 11 and 12 on Page 2 and 3). No genotyping of target markers was conducted in this study.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies were generated or presented for the sampled mosquitoes in this study.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from villages located in Jimma, TiroAfeta, OmoNada and Kerssa districts (weredas) in south-western Ethiopia, from November 2011 to January 2012 (Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary study evaluating the bio-efficacy of LLINs and synergistic CDC bottle bioassays on field-caught/reared mosquitoes (Page 1-3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Sampling took place in Jimma, TiroAfeta, OmoNada and Kerssa districts in south-western Ethiopia (latitudes 7°42'50"N to 07°53'50"N, longitudes 037°11'22"E to 037°20'36"E) (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from November 2011 to January 2012 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Field collection and bioassay data are newly presented for the Nov 2011 - Jan 2012 study period.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data needed; no genotyping was conducted in this study.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated pyrethroid susceptibility and the bio-efficacy of six WHO-recommended long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) using CDC bottle bioassays (with and without PBO) and WHO cone bioassays on field-collected Anopheles arabiensis from four districts in south-western Ethiopia. No molecular genotyping of resistance markers was performed in this study (bioassay-only paper).
exclusion_reasons: No target insecticide-resistance markers were genotyped in this study (bioassay-only paper).
